key_insight: A multimodal pretreatment model combining clinical, immune, tumor, transcriptomic, and genomic data predicted primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC better than single biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help identify patients less likely to benefit from checkpoint inhibitor-based treatment, supporting more personalized first-line or later-line therapy decisions.
method: Prospective multicenter study across 17 centers (PIONeeR; NCT03493581)
439 adults with advanced NSCLC profiled before treatment across six biological layers
Compared 36 feature-selection methods and 10 machine-learning models using .632 optimism-corrected validation
evidence_signal: The best multimodal signature achieved an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.73 ± 0.05 and PPV of 0.63 ± 0.07, outperforming PD-L1 and TMB alone.
watch_item: The signature still needs external validation and practical simplification before routine clinical implementation, especially given lower PPV in the first-line setting.
paper_title: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
